sections.title: Detailed Brief Overview
rows: **Legislative Amendments & Government of India Act 1935** — Constitutional milestones in British India leading to self-governance.
**1773 to 1935** — Spanning from the **Regulating Act of 1773** to the comprehensive **Government of India Act, 1935**.
British India / Westminster Parliament, London — Imposed on **Provinces** and **Princely States**.
British Parliament, Governor-Generals, Viceroys (**Lord Morley**, **Lord Minto**, **Lord Montagu**, **Lord Chelmsford**, **Lord Willingdon**).
Established the foundation for the **Indian Constitution**, introduced **Provincial Autonomy**, **Dyarchy**, and federal structures.
**1935 Act**: All-India Federation, abolition of provincial dyarchy, introduction of center dyarchy, creation of **RBI** and **Federal Court**.
High-scoring static GK section; questions frequently asked on **Morley-Minto Reforms (1909)**, **Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms (1919)**, and **1935 Act**.
**Act of 1935** contained **321 sections** and **10 schedules**; described by **Jawaharlal Nehru** as a "Charter of Slavery" and "Machine with all brakes, no engine".

items.title: Regulating Act 1773 & Pitt's India Act 1784
items.content:
• **Regulating Act 1773:** First step by British Parliament to control and regulate East India Company affairs in India.
• **Governor of Bengal** designated as **Governor-General of Bengal** (**Warren Hastings** was the first).
• **Supreme Court at Calcutta** established in **1774** (Chief Justice: **Sir Elijah Impey**).
• **Pitt's India Act 1784:** Established **Board of Control** (political affairs) alongside **Court of Directors** (commercial affairs), establishing **Double Government**.
• **Mnemonic for Acts:** **R**eady **P**lease (**R**egulating 1773, **P**itt's 1784).

items.title: Charter Acts: 1793, 1813, 1833, and 1853
items.content:
• **Charter Act 1813:** Ended EIC's trade monopoly in India (except tea and trade with China); allowed Christian missionaries.
• **Charter Act 1833:** **Governor-General of Bengal** made **Governor-General of India** (**Lord William Bentinck** was the first).
• Ended commercial activities of EIC completely; made it purely an administrative body.
• **Charter Act 1853:** Introduced open competition for civil services (**Macaulay Committee** appointed in **1854**).
• **Mnemonic for Charter Years:** **R**emember **E**very **C**harter **A**ct (**1793, 1813, 1833, 1853** — gap of 20 years except the last).

items.title: Government of India Act 1858 & Councils Acts
items.content:
• **Government of India Act 1858 (Good Government of India Act):** Abolished **East India Company**, transferred power to the **British Crown**.
• Created new office of **Secretary of State for India** (member of British cabinet) assisted by a **15-member Council**.
• Governor-General became known as **Viceroy** (**Lord Canning** was the first).
• **Indian Councils Act 1861:** Introduced **Portfolio system** and ordinance-making power for Viceroy.
• **Indian Councils Act 1892:** Increased non-official members in legislative councils; introduced indirect elections.
• **Mnemonic for Viceroys:** **C**anning **L**ytton **R**ipon **C**urzon (**C**ROWN acts).

items.title: Morley-Minto Reforms (Indian Councils Act 1909)
items.content:
• **Lord Morley** (Secretary of State) and **Lord Minto** (Viceroy).
• Significantly increased size of legislative councils (Central and Provincial).
• **Satyendra Prasad Sinha** became the first Indian to join the **Viceroy's Executive Council** (as Law Member).
• Introduced **Communal Electorate** for Muslims — **Lord Minto** recognized as the **Father of Communal Electorate**.
• **Mnemonic:** **M-M** = **M**orley-**M**into = **M**uslim Electorate.

items.title: Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms (Government of India Act 1919)
items.content:
• **Edwin Montagu** (Secretary of State) and **Lord Chelmsford** (Viceroy).
• Introduced **Dyarchy** (dual rule) in provinces: subjects divided into **Transferred** (administered by Governor with ministers) and **Reserved** (administered by Governor with executive council).
• Introduced **Bicameralism** at the Center for the first time (Council of State and Legislative Assembly).
• Provided for establishment of a **Public Service Commission** (set up in **1926**).
• Provided for appointment of a statutory commission after 10 years (**Simon Commission**).
• **Mnemonic:** **1919** = **D**yarchy in **P**rovinces (**D**P).

items.title: Government of India Act 1935
items.content:
• Provided for establishment of an **All-India Federation** comprising provinces and princely states (did not come into effect as princely states did not join).
• Abolished **Dyarchy in provinces** and introduced **Provincial Autonomy**.
• Introduced **Dyarchy at the Center** (Federal subjects divided into Reserved and Transferred).
• Introduced **Bicameralism** in 6 out of 11 provinces (Assam, Bengal, Bihar, Bombay, Madras, United Provinces).
• Established **Federal Court** (set up in **1937** in Delhi) and **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**.
• Separated **Burma (Myanmar)** from India and created new provinces **Sindh** and **Orissa**.
• **Mnemonic:** **35** = **A**utonomy, **F**ederation, **R**BI (**A**ll **F**ine **R**ules).

items.definition: Remember **B**engal to **I**ndia to **C**rown: **B**engal (Warren Hastings, 1773) -> **I**ndia (William Bentinck, 1833) -> **C**rown/Viceroy (Lord Canning, 1858).
Associate **Minto** with **M**uslim electorate — **M**into = **M**uslim communal representation in **1909**.
Dyarchy started in **Provinces** in **1919** (Mont-Ford) and moved to **Center** in **1935** (Provincial Autonomy granted).
Charter Acts were passed every **20 years**: **1793**, **1813**, **1833**, and **1853**.
Remember **B-B-M-A-B-U**: **B**engal, **B**ihar, **M**adras, **A**ssam, **B**ombay, **U**nited Provinces (6 provinces out of 11 got bicameral legislatures).
Remember **R-F-F**: **R**BI, **F**ederal Court, **F**ederal Public Service Commission.

items.term: Mistake 1: Confusing First Governor-General of Bengal vs India
items.definition: **Warren Hastings** was Governor-General of **Bengal** (1773). **Lord William Bentinck** was Governor-General of **India** (1833).
The first **Viceroy of India** was **Lord Canning** (under the 1858 Act), whereas the last Governor-General under the Company was also Lord Canning.
Students often confuse where dyarchy was introduced. It was introduced in **Provinces in 1919** and abolished in provinces while introduced at the **Center in 1935**.
**Morley-Minto** is **1909** (Muslim Electorate). **Montagu-Chelmsford** is **1919** (Dyarchy & Bicameral Center). Do not interchange them.

items.term: Mistake 5: Establishment Year of RBI and Federal Court
items.definition: While the **Government of India Act** was passed in **1935**, the **RBI** was established in **1935** and the **Federal Court** started functioning in **1937**.
The All-India Federation proposed in the **1935 Act** **never came into operation** because the Princely States refused to join it.
First parliamentary intervention; Supreme Court at Calcutta; Governor-General of Bengal.
Created Board of Control, establishing a dual system of British control over company affairs.
Abolished EIC monopoly on Indian trade (except tea and China trade).
Made Governor-General of Bengal the Governor-General of India (**Lord William Bentinck**).
Introduced open civil service examinations; Macaulay Committee report of 1854.
Transferred governance to the British Crown; created Secretary of State and Viceroy.
Introduced portfolio system and ordinance-making power for the Viceroy.
Expanded legislative councils with indirect election elements.
Introduced separate/communal electorates for Muslims; Satyendra Prasad Sinha joined executive council.
Introduced provincial dyarchy and bicameral legislature at the center.
Provided provincial autonomy, federal court, RBI, bicameralism in 6 provinces, and center dyarchy.

upscNotes.content: In UPSSSC PET, focus heavily on the matching questions pairing Acts with their respective Viceroys/Secretaries of State and key features like communal electorates or dyarchy.
Memorize the exact years of the Charter Acts (1793, 1813, 1833, 1853) as questions frequently test the 20-year interval pattern.
Students often get trapped thinking the All-India Federation under the 1935 Act was successfully implemented. Remember, it failed because Princely States opted out.
Do not confuse the transfer of power date: Company rule ended in 1858, not 1857 (the year of the Revolt).
Note that Burma was officially separated from British India through a provision in the Government of India Act, 1935.

keyTakeaways: Regulating Act of 1773 was the foundational step of British parliamentary control in India.
Act of 1858 shifted power directly from the East India Company to the British Crown.
Morley-Minto Reforms (1909) introduced communal electorates, sowing the seeds of partition.
Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms (1919) introduced dyarchy in provinces and bicameralism at the center.
Government of India Act (1935) was the blueprint for independent India's Constitution, introducing provincial autonomy and the Federal Court.
RBI and Federal Court were significant economic and judicial outcomes tied to the 1935 legislative framework.
